# Citation

Song, D., et al. (2023). *scDesign3 generates realistic in silico data for multimodal single-cell and spatial omics*. Nature Biotechnology. DOI: 10.1038/s41587-023-01772-1. Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11182337/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11182337/).

# One-Sentence Summary

Presents scDesign3, a reference-based framework for realistic single-cell, multi-omic, and spatial-omics simulation.

# Scope for simitall

Use as an advanced, reference-based option when users have a real single-cell or spatial dataset and want technical realism beyond a parametric toy dataset.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Reference-based simulation can retain complex feature and cell-level dependencies.
- Covariates such as cell state, condition, and spatial location can be represented explicitly.
- The reference dataset must be appropriate for the intended biological setting.

# Inputs to Specify

- Reference single-cell or spatial data
- Cell metadata and covariates
- Requested modality and sample design

# Expected Outputs

- Synthetic count or multimodal matrices
- Cell-level covariates
- Simulation configuration

# Limitations and Guardrails

- A simulator can reproduce reference patterns but cannot establish causal biology absent from the reference.
- Avoid treating simulated spatial structure as experimentally validated tissue organization.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- When should a workflow choose a reference-based scRNA-seq simulator?
- What real data are needed for a credible spatial-omics simulation?
